Heat and light are relatively easy to manage, but water is another matter. If the power goes out, so does your well, unless you are lucky enough to have a hand-dug shallow well with good water. City water supplies will probably also fail when the electricity goes out.

You can pump water using wind power, and store it in an elevated cistern for when the wind doesn't blow. That gives you constant water pressure. But you run into the problem of freezing if you live in a northern part of the world. Keeping an elevated cistern from freezing is difficult. The best way is to put it into your house, which you will heat with wood or some other source. The pipes leading from the well need to be insulated or underground as well.
